controls.name: (ACCESS CONTROL) POLICY AND PROCEDURES – Included in the Privacy

fields.label: Justification to Select for ACCT, Low, Moderate, and High
fields.text: Account management is a critical function for developing and implementing an access control framework that is appropriate for the information contained in systems and applications. When implemented effectively, the access control framework provides the necessary constructs for controlling access to PII, limiting disclosure of records about individuals to only those system and application users that have a need for the information to perform their job functions. Organizations should provide access only to the minimum amount of PII necessary for users to perform their duties.

fields.label: Guidance
fields.text: Use of temporary accounts is prohibited for accessing PII as these accounts have increased risk and little or no accountability.

controls.name: Account Management | Automated System Account Management

fields.label: Justification to Select for Moderate and High

fields.text: Automated mechanisms protect privacy by providing stronger assurance than manual approaches that access to the PII is appropriately managed. Temporary and emergency accounts may allow access to PII that differs from on-going access requirements. Automating the process of removing or disabling temporary and emergency accounts helps ensure that access controls return to normal within a reasonable and intended timeframe.

fields.label: Justification to Select for Low, Moderate, and High
fields.text: Protects privacy by ensuring access to the PII is limited to those individuals who are permitted and have a need to know the information. Privileged users play a critical role in implementing access controls that protect PII. They also support program and system owners with understanding the access control options that are available in their environment.

fields.label: Justification to Not Select for ACCT, Low, Moderate, or High
fields.text: Systems that process PII must not select this control without first coordinating with the SAOP or designee. Access to PII may not be granted to entities who are previously unknown, but rather only to officers and employees who have a need for the information in performance of their duties. Dynamic account creation is an automated process that may not support independent verification of a need for access to PII.

controls.name: Account Management | Restrictions on Use of Shared and Group Accounts

fields.label: Justification to Select for ACCT, Low, Moderate, and High
fields.text: Shared and group accounts are permitted for systems that process PII only with explicit approval by the SAOP, or designee.

fields.label: Parameter Value
fields.text: Only permit the use of shared and group accounts that meet explicit approval by the SAOP or designee.

controls.name: Account Management | Account Monitoring for Atypical Usage

fields.label: Justification to Select for ACCT, Low, Moderate, and High
fields.text: Atypical use of systems with PII may be an indicator of a privacy incident or breach.

fields.label: Guidance
fields.text: Atypical use that involves PII should be reported to the SAOP, or designee, for further evaluation.

fields.label: Reference(s)
fields.text: 5 USC 552a(e)(10), OMB M-17-12, OMB Circular A-130

controls.name: Account Management | Disable Accounts for High-Risk Individuals

fields.label: Justification to Select for ACCT, Low, Moderate, and High
fields.text: Disabling accounts for high- risk individuals is a minimum requirement to be included in the organization’s rules of behavior as a consequence for abusing access privileges to access PII, including information protected under the Privacy Act of 1974.

fields.label: Justification to Select for ACCT, Low, Moderate, and High
fields.text: Organizations shall control access to PII through access enforcement mechanisms. Well-designed, automated access controls (e.g., mandatory access control (MAC), discretionary access control (DAC), role-based access control (RBAC), or attribute-based access control (ABAC)) limit user access to information according to defined access policies, which helps ensure the security and confidentiality of the PII processed by the system.

fields.label: Guidance
fields.text: For example, implement role-based access controls and configure access controls so that each user can access only the pieces of information necessary for the user’s role or only permit users to access PII through an application that restricts their access to the PII the users require, instead of allowing users direct access to a database or files containing PII.

fields.label: Reference(s)
fields.text: 5 U.S.C. §552a(b), (e)(9)-(10); EO 14028 Sec 3(a), Sec 4(a-b), e(i)(C), (g) AC-3(9) Access Enforcement | Controlled Release

fields.label: Justification to Select for ACCT, Low, Moderate, and High
fields.text: PII released outside a system boundary may be at increased risk of unauthorized access and use. Release includes both formal, documented processes and informal activities, such as providing a spreadsheet to an external entity that was created using data extracted from a system.

fields.label: Moderate and High Parameter Value
fields.text: Release information outside of the system only if: (a) The receiving organization or system provides privacy and security controls commensurate with the privacy risk level of the PII being received; and (b) Controls PT-3 and AC-21 are used to validate the appropriateness of the information designated for release.

fields.label: Reference(s)
fields.text: 5 U.S.C. §552a(a)(7), (b), (c), (e)(3)(c), (e)(10)(o); FISA; EO 12333; Privacy and Civil Liberties Implementation Guide for the Information Sharing Environment, Version 1.0, www.ise.gov

controls.name: Access Enforcement | Audited Override of Access Control Mechanisms*

fields.label: Justification to Recommend for Privacy Enhancing
fields.text: Overrides of Access Control Mechanisms create a situation where users are permitted access to systems during emergency situations who under normal circumstances would not have system access or privileges. This open access creates the potential for the individual to have access to PII. Auditing access control overrides provides a way of identifying and addressing privacy issues that may occur as a result of the override.

controls.name: Access Enforcement | Restrict Access to Specific Information Types*

fields.label: Justification to Recommend for Privacy Enhancing
fields.text: Protects privacy by providing granular access to specific, limited information.

fields.label: Justification to Recommend for Privacy Enhancing
fields.text: Provides increased controls to further enforce access requirements for PII to ensure access is limited to those individuals who are permitted and have a need to know the information.

fields.label: Reference(s)
fields.text: FISA, EO 12333

fields.label: Justification to Select for ACCT, Low, Moderate, and High
fields.text: The Individual Participation Fair Information Practice Principle (FIPP) requires organizations to provide mechanisms for individuals to gain access to their PII when appropriate. The Privacy Act of 1974, as amended, requires organizations to provide mechanisms for individuals to gain access to their PII when that PII meets the definition of a “record.” Some systems may be exempted from this requirement when statutory requirements are met. Access is also an important aspect of supporting correction of PII and redress against alleged violations and misuse of their PII.

fields.label: Guidance
fields.text: Provide for public access to records, including PII not included in a Privacy Act System of Records, where required or appropriate. While the language of this control is specific to the Privacy Act's requirements for access, FIPPs encourage organizations to use available authorities to provide access when the Privacy Act does not apply. For example, some organizations use the Freedom of Information Act as another tool to provide access to PII for an affected individual. Also select for Privacy Act System of Records that do not have exemptions.

fields.label: Reference(s)
fields.text: 5 U.S.C. §552a(c)(3), (c)(4), (d), and (h); FISA; EO 12333; OMB Circular A-130

fields.label: Justification to Select for ACCT, Low, Moderate, and High
fields.text: The information flow enforcement controls provide a technical means of implementing disclosure requirements by minimizing information shared between networks, devices, and individuals within systems and between interconnected systems. This control can also limit information transfers between organizations based on data structures and content.

controls.name: Information Flow Enforcement | Object Security and Privacy Attributes*

fields.label: Justification to Recommend for Privacy Enhancing
fields.text: Enhances privacy protection by requiring PII to be tagged for identification and protects information in transit with flow enforcement preventing the PII from being moved to a system not authorized to host PII. For example, a record containing PII may be flagged with an attribute that indicates sharing the PII is not permitted. A system can then be configured to take actions such as excluding the record when sharing a group of records from the system.

fields.label: Justification to Recommend for Privacy Enhancing
fields.text: Processing domains can support privacy risk management by providing a location that uses more restrictive privacy controls beyond those that may be required for other processing environments. This can help organizations meet their objectives while more efficiently using their resources (e.g., controls may be less expensive to employ in a smaller, restricted domain than across the entire network).

controls.name: Information Flow Enforcement | Security and Privacy Policy Filters*

fields.label: Justification to Recommend for Privacy Enhancing
fields.text: Security and privacy policy filtering technology, such as data loss prevention (DLP), can provide a form of continuous monitoring for compliance with privacy laws and regulations. Implementation of this control reduces the potential for unauthorized transfer of PII.

fields.label: Parameter Value
fields.text: (a) Enforce information flow control using best available security and/or privacy policy filters, or like technology to filter on selected PII values as a basis for flow control decisions for prevention of unauthorized transfer of PII across system boundaries or domains;

controls.name: Information Flow Enforcement | Detection of Unsanctioned Information*

fields.label: Justification to Recommend for Privacy Enhancing
fields.text: To provide the ability for an organization to monitor and prevent transfer of PII across different security domains, a system needs to have mechanisms to automatically detect, and where appropriate, prohibit the unauthorized transfer of PII across different security domains. Typical implementations of such controls will detect particular data types or metadata tagging and take action to prevent the transfer of the information beyond the ended boundaries.

fields.label: Guidance
fields.text: The organization provides the capability for the organization to centrally monitor for and detect unauthorized transfer of such PII across different security domains. Some technologies that would facilitate this include data-loss prevention, data- rights management, and key-word detection to prevent the unauthorized export of information from a network or to render such information unusable in the event of the unauthorized export of such information between security domains.

fields.label: Justification to Recommend for Privacy Enhancing
fields.text: The ability to identify source and destination points for PII flow within systems is necessary for attribution and compliance with need to know requirements.

fields.label: Guidance
fields.text: Implement a higher level of granularity for identification and authentication based on sensitivity of the PII. This is not to determine permissibility of the transfer but to enable an audit capability.

fields.label: Parameter Value
fields.text: Uniquely identify and authenticate source and destination points by the applicable organization, system, application, or individual for information transfer.

fields.label: Justification to Select for ACCT, Low, Moderate, and High
fields.text: Separation of duties aligns privileges with appropriate roles with the idea that duties are split between roles in such a way as to reduce the risk of malevolent or inappropriate behaviors based on access. Implementing this control helps reduce the risk of inappropriate access to PII (e.g., separating employees that perform security investigations from mission and business functions).

fields.label: Guidance
fields.text: Separation of duties is implemented by designating a selected set of administrators the capability to set user permissions to PII information, while those administrators do not themselves have access to the PII. The principle of separation of duties is significant for developers as well as for operational system administrators.

fields.label: Justification to Select for ACCT, Low, Moderate, and High
fields.text: Limit access to PII to designated individuals with a need-to-know in performance of their job duties.

fields.label: Guidance
fields.text: Enforce the most restrictive set of rights/privileges or access needed by users (or processes acting on behalf of users) for the performance of specified tasks — increasing the level of restriction as privacy risk level rises. The organization ensures that users who must access records containing PII only have access to the minimum amount of PII, along with only those privileges (e.g., read, write, execute) necessary to perform their assigned tasks.

fields.label: Reference(s)
fields.text: 5 U.S.C. §552a(b); NIST SP 800-122; CNSSD No. 504

controls.name: Least Privilege | Authorize Access to Security Functions

fields.label: Justification to Select for Moderate and High
fields.text: Limit access to security functions to authorized personnel to reduce the number of users able to perform certain security functions, such as configuring access permissions, setting audit logs, performing system management functions. Examples of authorized personnel include security administrators, system and network administrators, system security officers, system maintenance personnel, system programmers, and other privileged users. These types of security functions can provide a level of access to PII, and capabilities to manipulate it, in ways that other user roles typically could not.

fields.label: Guidance
fields.text: Identify the security relevant functions that require authorized access for all systems that contain Moderate or High PII.

fields.label: Reference(s)
fields.text: 5 U.S.C. §552a(b)(1); NIST SP 800-205; CNSSD No. 504

controls.name: Least Privilege | Non-Privileged Access for Non-Security Functions

fields.label: Justification to Select for ACCT, Low, Moderate, and High
fields.text: System users with elevated privileges use non-privileged accounts when performing non-security functions. Requiring system users to use their non-privileged accounts when working with PII for purposes other than security functions limits inadvertent access to or disclosure of PII and protects the integrity of PII.

fields.label: Guidance
fields.text: Any access involving PII that is non-administrative in nature should require the user to use their non-privileged accounts to perform that function.

fields.label: Reference(s)
fields.text: 5 U.S.C. §552a(b); EO 14028 Sec 4(i); CNSSD No. 504

controls.name: Least Privilege | Network Access to Privileged Commands*

fields.label: Justification to Recommend for Privacy Enhancing
fields.text: Limiting access and documenting the justification for this operational need provides an added layer of privacy protection by further reducing and clarifying the individuals who have access to the PII. By restricting access to specific commands, it limits inadvertent access to or disclosure of PII and protects the integrity of PII.

fields.label: Reference(s)
fields.text: 5 U.S.C. §552a(b); EO 14028 Sec 4(i); CNSSD No. 504

fields.label: Justification to Select for ACCT, Low, Moderate, and High
fields.text: This control limits who is authorized to have administrative accounts, such as those who can perform security functions to include configuring access permissions, setting audit log collection events and performing system management functions. These types of system and network management personnel typically have a level of access that is capable of circumventing other access controls. Limiting access to these accounts further protects PII by limiting the number of individuals that have the “keys to the kingdom” on a network or system.

fields.label: Reference(s)
fields.text: 5 U.S.C. §552a(b)(1); FISA; EO 12333; EO 14028 Sec 4(i)(k); CNSSD No. 504

controls.name: Least Privilege | Review of User Privileges

fields.label: Justification to Select for ACCT, Low, Moderate, and High
fields.text: Review of user privileges is necessary in order to ensure privileges are revoked for those who no longer require access to PII. Implementation of this control reduces the risk of unauthorized access to PII by users who no longer need access to perform their job functions.

fields.label: ACCT, Low, and Moderate Parameter Value
fields.text: (a) Review at least annually the privileges assigned to individuals with access to low or moderate PII or ACCT PII to validate the need for such privileges;

fields.label: High Parameter Value
fields.text: (a) Review at least quarterly the privileges assigned to individuals with access to privileged accounts and at least annually the privileges assigned to individuals with access to high PII to validate the need for such privileges;

controls.name: Least Privilege | Privilege Levels for Code Execution

fields.label: Justification to Select for ACCT, Low, Moderate, and High
fields.text: Ensure system software does not allow users to obtain elevated privileges (and potentially access to PII beyond what the individual requires in performance of their job duties).

fields.label: Guidance
fields.text: Enforce the most restrictive set of rights/privileges or access needed by users (or processes acting on behalf of users) for the performance of specified tasks — increasing the level of restriction as privacy risk level rises. Users who must access records containing PII should only have access to the minimum amount of PII and privileges (e.g., read, write, execute) necessary to perform their assigned tasks.

fields.label: Reference(s)
fields.text: 5 U.S.C. §552a(b); OMB Circular A-130; CNSSD No. 504

controls.name: Least Privilege | Log Use of Privileged Functions

fields.label: Justification to Select for Moderate and High
fields.text: Privileged functions have elevated permissions to access, and grant access, to PII. Accountability requires the ability to detect, trace, and audit a privileged function whenever it is executed.

fields.label: Reference(s)
fields.text: 5 U.S.C. §552a(b); FISA; EO 12333; EO 14028 Sec 4(e)(i)(B); OMB Circular A-130; CNSSD No. 504

controls.name: Least Privilege | Prohibit Non-Privileged Users from Executing Privileged

fields.label: Justification to Select for ACCT, Low, Moderate, and High
fields.text: Non-privileged users may not have the same level of trust as privileged users. Privileged functions have access beyond that of the typical user, and as such may have greater ability to access PII. Individual accountability requires the ability to trace (audit) the actions of the user who initiated them.

fields.label: Reference(s)
fields.text: OMB Circular A-130; CNSSD No. 504

controls.name: SYSTEM USE NOTIFICATION – Included in Privacy Control Baseline

fields.label: Justification to Select for ACCT, Low, Moderate, and High
fields.text: Protect PII from unauthorized access when system users are away from their workstation. Session lock for remote and mobile devices is neither technically nor financially burdensome. Based on risk, many agencies have adopted 15-minute session locks by policy as a best practice. Period of inactivity shall be no more than 30 minutes before session lock occurs for remote and mobile devices and requires user re-authentication.

fields.label: Parameter Value
fields.text: a. Prevent further access to the system by initiating a device lock after a period not to exceed 30 minutes of inactivity, requiring the user to initiate a device lock before leaving the system unattended;

fields.label: Justification to Select for Moderate and High
fields.text: Implementation of this control provides a technical means to enforce security and privacy policies, e.g., access controls and encryption. Meta-data that supports privacy attributes is required to properly determine whether access to PII should be granted.

fields.label: Guidance
fields.text: Use privacy attributes including, as a minimum, completion of privacy training and clear identification of data structures containing (or planned to contain) PII to enable cross system functionality and reciprocity through consistent privacy attribute interpretation. This control supports privacy protections by assigning privacy attributes that characterize information, devices, or processes (i.e., an “object”) as containing PII or associate an organization’s mandatory security/privacy training requirement with a user of a system containing PII (i.e., a “subject”). Security and privacy…

fields.label: Parameter Value
fields.text: a. Provide the means to associate a privacy attribute to demonstrate the user (subject) has completed privacy training in the last year with a privacy attribute of “Contains PII” having a value of “yes” or “no” for data structures that are known or plan to contain PII for information in storage, in process, and/or in transmission;

fields.label: Reference(s)
fields.text: 5 U.S.C. §552a(b), (e)(9)-(10); OMB Circular A-130

controls.name: Security and Privacy Attributes | Maintenance of Attribute Associations by

fields.label: Justification to Select for ACCT, Low, Moderate, and High
fields.text: Maintaining the association and integrity of security attributes to subjects and objects can be used as the basis of automated policy actions, such as intrusion detection and keyword detection tools.

fields.label: Parameter Value
fields.text: Maintain the association and integrity of the user attribute of “Annual PII Training” for individuals with access to PII to the information attribute of “Contains PII” to applicable information.

fields.label: Reference(s)
fields.text: 5 U.S.C. §552a(b) and (e)(9)-(10); OMB Circular A-130

fields.label: Justification to Select for ACCT, Low, Moderate, and High
fields.text: Limiting access to PII from remote networks and/or restricting activities that can be conducted with PII remotely reduces the risk of intentional and unintentional disclosures of PII that may not exist on an internal network.

fields.label: Guidance
fields.text: Allow remote access to PII only with two-factor authentication where one of the factors is provided by a device separate from the computer gaining access.

fields.label: Justification to Select for ACCT, Low, Moderate, and High
fields.text: Auditing remote access ensures unauthorized connections to systems containing PII can be detected across all system platforms (e.g., servers, mobile devices, workstations).

fields.label: Guidance
fields.text: Audit all remote access to, and actions on, resources containing PII.

controls.name: Remote Access | Protection of Confidentiality and Integrity Using Encryption

fields.label: Justification to Select for ACCT, Low, Moderate, and High
fields.text: Encrypting remote sessions protects the confidentiality and integrity of PII.

fields.label: Justification to Select for ACCT, Low, Moderate, and High
fields.text: Authentication is necessary to know who accesses the PII. Communications over wireless networks, unless properly secured, have greater risk of interception than hard-wired networks. Implementing encryption of wireless network communications containing PII renders any intercepted data unreadable.

fields.label: Guidance
fields.text: If wireless networks permit access to organization systems containing PII, then encryption of content and authentication of users or devices is required. Organizations should ensure that all wireless local area network (WLAN) components use Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS)-validated cryptographic algorithms to protect the confidentiality and integrity of WLAN communications and NSA-approved cryptographic algorithms to protect the confidentiality and integrity of classified WLAN communications.

fields.label: Reference(s)
fields.text: 5 U.S.C. §552a(b), (e)(10); OMB Circular A-130; NIST SP 800-97, NIST SP 800-153

fields.label: Justification to Select for Low, Moderate, and High
fields.text: Limiting access to PII from mobile devices reduces the risk of intentional and unintentional disclosures of PII that may not exist on an internal network.

fields.label: Guidance
fields.text: Encrypt information on all mobile devices that contains low, moderate, and high PII.

fields.label: Reference(s)
fields.text: OMB Circular A-130; OMB M-17-12

controls.name: Access Control for Mobile Devices | Full Device or Container-Based Encryption

fields.label: Justification to Select for Low, Moderate, and High
fields.text: Mobile devices are more likely to be lost or stolen and as a result PII is more vulnerable. Encryption reduces this vulnerability.

fields.label: Guidance
fields.text: Encrypt information on all mobile devices that contains low, moderate, and high PII.

fields.label: Parameter Value
fields.text: Employ full-device encryption or container encryption to protect the confidentiality and integrity of information on any type of mobile device permitted by the organization to access PII.

fields.label: Reference(s)
fields.text: 5 U.S.C. §552a(e)(10); OMB Circular A-130

fields.label: Justification to Select for ACCT, Low, Moderate, and High
fields.text: Access to PII from external systems (including, but not limited to, personally owned systems/devices) increases risk of loss of the data. Reinforce by a binding agreement to terms and conditions of the organization’s privacy requirements to ensure awareness and accountability of both parties. Privacy requirements shall be addressed in agreements that cover relationships in which external systems are used to access, process, store, or transmit and manage PII. Access to PII from external systems (including, but not limited to, personally owned systems/devices) is limited to those organizations…

fields.label: Guidance
fields.text: Such agreements may include memoranda of understanding (MOUs), terms of service, or contracts.

fields.label: Reference(s)
fields.text: 5 U.S.C. §552a(e)(10); FAR Part 24, 39.105; OMB Circular A-130

controls.name: Use of External Systems | Limits on Authorized Use

fields.label: Justification to Select for Low, Moderate, and High
fields.text: Access to PII from external systems increases risk of loss of the data. An external system which processes, stores, or transmits PII needs to have its security and privacy controls verified to meet the organization's security control requirements for systems processing PII.

fields.label: Reference(s)
fields.text: 5 U.S.C. §552a(e)(10); FAR Part 24, 39.105; OMB Circular A-130

controls.name: Use of External Systems | Non-Organizationally Owned Systems — Restricted

fields.label: Justification to Select for Low, Moderate, and High
fields.text: This control is needed to implement protections for PII contained on any device not owned by the organization, including personal mobile devices, commonly referred to as “bring your own device” (BYOD). Mobile devices are more vulnerable to loss or theft than other types of computing media (e.g., desktops and servers) due to their portability and widespread use inside and outside of government facilities. PII stored on mobile devices is more vulnerable as a result. At a minimum, controls must include implementation of either full-device or virtual container encryption to reduce the…

fields.label: Guidance
fields.text: The organization should include in its mobile strategy a method to ensure both the device’s access to PII can be revoked and the device’s PII contents can be remotely removed.

fields.label: Parameter Value
fields.text: Restrict the use of non-organizationally owned systems or system components to process organizational information using PII.

fields.label: Reference(s)
fields.text: 5 U.S.C. §552a(e)(10); OMB M-17-12; OMB Circular A-130

fields.label: Justification to Select for ACCT, Low, Moderate, and High
fields.text: PII protected by the Privacy Act may not be disclosed without first providing notice to the individuals about whom the information will be disclosed and for what purpose. When PII is shared it is necessary to ensure the PII is being shared in accordance with statutory and regulatory requirements, including any restrictions on how the PII may be shared and the receiving partner’s security requirements. Sharing PII with third parties introduces new risks to the individual which, as applicable, requires organizations to establish formal agreements with the third party and ensure the sharing is…

fields.label: Guidance
fields.text: This control addresses the sharing of information in a general sense (i.e., disclosure). It is not “information sharing” as defined by the Information Sharing Environment (ISE) Privacy Guidelines. All sharing partners, processes, and systems must comply with applicable SORN, Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA), or other forms of notice or public statements. Consistent with the Purpose Specification and Use Limitation FIPPs, sharing of PII must be compatible with the purpose for which it was collected. Consistent with the Transparency FIPP, any subsequent sharing that is not compatible or…

fields.label: Justification to Select for ACCT, Low, Moderate, and High
fields.text: PII may only be disclosed through appropriate channels. fields.text: EO 13526 directs the safeguarding of classified information while in use and when transmitted to provide adequate protection and prevent access by unauthorized persons. fields.text: Collaborative devices have an aspect of trust associated with their use (e.g., it is hard to verify how many people are listening through one connection).
